[Turn 1 USER]
e001	I lead operations at a profitable software company and have been offered the chief operating role at a climate startup founded by someone I trust.
e002	The startup's mission matters to me, and the role would be broader than my current job, but it has fourteen months of runway and no repeatable sales process.
e003	My current company has offered me a larger team and a retention grant if I stay.
e004	My partner is starting a demanding training program in the autumn, so predictability at home is not an abstract benefit.
e005	I keep moving between “this is the moment to do consequential work” and “I am romanticizing scope because my current role has become familiar.”
[Turn 1 ASSISTANT]
e006	The choice mixes at least three questions: whether the startup is a sound operating bet, whether the role fits the work you want, and whether this is a workable year for your household.
e007	A bigger title does not prove broader authority if the founder has not clarified decisions or if fundraising dominates the job.
e008	Stability is not automatically fear, but the retention package can make staying look more intentional than it is.
e009	Before choosing, separate what you need to learn about the company from what you need to negotiate with your partner and current employer.
[Turn 7 USER]
e054	I am leaning toward proposing the twelve-week project while staying at eighty percent in my current role, with the household schedule written down before it starts.
e055	I will tell the founder that successful collaboration would make me seriously consider joining, but I am not willing to resign unless the financing extends runway beyond eighteen months and we agree how pricing conflicts are decided.
e056	I also want my current CEO to understand that I may leave rather than presenting the arrangement as professional development.
e057	I have not resolved whether asking for the trial is already a decision to leave in practice, even if it is not one formally.
[Turn 7 ASSISTANT]
e058	The plan distinguishes a decision to run a bounded test from willingness to accept the full-time role.
e059	Your financing, authority, and household conditions make that distinction more concrete, while candor with your CEO reduces the risk of calling a departure process “development.”
e060	The trial can reveal how you and the founder work and whether the schedule is livable.
e061	It cannot fully test post-fundraising pressure or prevent either organization from treating the trial as a directional commitment.
